	<item>
		<title>Under Glass Cloches, Amber Cowan Nests Enchanting Flameworked Scenes</title>
		<link>https://www.thisiscolossal.com/2026/08/amber-cowan-glass-cloche-coupe-sculptures/</link>
		
		<dc:creator><![CDATA[Grace Ebert]]></dc:creator>
		<pubDate>Fri, 07 Aug 2026 19:12:25 +0000</pubDate>
				<category><![CDATA[Art]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[Amber Cowan]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[assemblage]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[flowers]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[glass]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[sculpture]]></category>
		<guid isPermaLink="false">https://www.thisiscolossal.com/?p=476594</guid>

					<description><![CDATA[<p><img src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/cowan-7.jpg" alt="Under Glass Cloches, Amber Cowan Nests Enchanting Flameworked Scenes" />Known for her lush assemblages of flameworked glass, Amber Cowan reimagines a ubiquitous medium.</p>

]]></description>
										<content:encoded><![CDATA[<img src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/cowan-7.jpg" alt="Under Glass Cloches, Amber Cowan Nests Enchanting Flameworked Scenes" />


<p>Known for <a href="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/tags/amber-cowan/">her lush assemblages</a> of flameworked glass, <a href="https://ambercowan.com/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Amber Cowan</a> reimagines a ubiquitous yet fragile medium. Flowers, filigree, and colorful baubles cluster into dense compositions that invoke fairytale narratives and whimsical nature scenes. Cowan typically works with industrial scraps, antiques, and other offcasts, which allows her to draw on products and colorways that are no longer in production.</p>



<p>Currently leaning into cloche and coupe sculptures alongside her wall-based works, the Philadelphia-based artist is preparing for several upcoming exhibitions, including at San Francisco&#8217;s Museum of Craft and Design in September and Design Miami in December. Her work is on view now in&nbsp;<em>The Passion of Collecting</em> at The Baker Museum in Naples, Florida, and you can find more on <a href="https://www.instagram.com/amber.cowan/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Instagram</a>.</p>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img fetchpriority="high" decoding="async" width="2000" height="2524" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/cowan-1.jpg" alt="a colorful milk glass coupe with swans, flowers, and other baubles under a clear glass cloche" class="wp-image-476595" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/cowan-1.jpg 2000w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/cowan-1-640x808.jpg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/cowan-1-960x1212.jpg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/cowan-1-768x969.jpg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/cowan-1-1217x1536.jpg 1217w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/cowan-1-1623x2048.jpg 1623w" sizes="(max-width: 2000px) 100vw, 2000px" /><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">&#8220;Swans in Delphite and Rosalene&#8221; (2026), 11 x 8 x 8 inches. 		<item>
		<title>A Menagerie of Animal Sculptures by 50+ Artists Populate &#8216;The Ark&#8217;</title>
		<link>https://www.thisiscolossal.com/2026/08/the-ark-powerhouse-arts-animal-sculptures-exhibition/</link>
		
		<dc:creator><![CDATA[Kate Mothes]]></dc:creator>
		<pubDate>Fri, 07 Aug 2026 15:07:34 +0000</pubDate>
				<category><![CDATA[Art]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[Climate]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[animals]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[sculpture]]></category>
		<guid isPermaLink="false">https://www.thisiscolossal.com/?p=476575</guid>

					<description><![CDATA[<p><img src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/ark-9.jpeg" alt="A Menagerie of Animal Sculptures by 50+ Artists Populate &#8216;The Ark&#8217;" />Powerhouse Arts asks, will we care for the future of our planet the way we care for the animals we love?</p>
<p>Do stories and artists like this matter to you? Become a <a href="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/members">Colossal Member</a> today and support independent arts publishing for as little as $7 per month. The article <a href="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/2026/08/the-ark-powerhouse-arts-animal-sculptures-exhibition/">A Menagerie of Animal Sculptures by 50+ Artists Populate &#8216;The Ark&#8217;</a> appeared first on <a href="https://www.thisiscolossal.com">Colossal</a>.</p>
]]></description>
										<content:encoded><![CDATA[<img src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/ark-9.jpeg" alt="A Menagerie of Animal Sculptures by 50+ Artists Populate &#8216;The Ark&#8217;" />


<p>The term &#8220;ark&#8221; invariably conjures images of the monumental boat onto which pairs of animals were stewarded prior to a cataclysmic, biblical flood. It&#8217;s a reference that feels apt amid the climate crisis and our planet&#8217;s <a href="https://www.climate.gov/news-features/understanding-climate/climate-change-global-sea-level" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">rising sea levels</a>, although in this case, the melting ice caps and creeping tides are down to us. The large-scale exhibition titled <em>The Ark</em> at <a href="https://powerhousearts.org/?" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Powerhouse Arts</a> asks, will we care for the future of our planet the way we care for the animals we love?</p>



<p>The presentation draws directly on the myth if The Deluge from <a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genesis_flood_narrative" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Genesis</a>, &#8220;an event of epic scale that becomes a metaphor for the present moment, where environmental and social upheaval converge,&#8221; says a statement. &#8220;Throughout the exhibition—experienced in the round, in close proximity, and at monumental scale—the animals function as both protagonists and interlocutors.&#8221;</p>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="2000" height="1333" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/ark-4.jpg" alt="an exhibition view of the large group exhibition 'The Ark' featuring animal sculptures by more than 50 artists" class="wp-image-476579" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/ark-4.jpg 2000w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/ark-4-640x427.jpg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/ark-4-960x640.jpg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/ark-4-768x512.jpg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/ark-4-1536x1024.jpg 1536w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 2000px) 100vw, 2000px" /><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">Installation view of &#8216;The Ark&#8217; at Powerhouse Arts, Summer 2026. Photo by Xavier Petromelis</figcaption></figure>



<p>Colossal readers may recognize the work of <a href="/tags/kiki-smith">Kiki Smith</a>, <a href="/tags/nichola-theakston">Nichola Theakston</a>, <a href="/tags/anthony-theakston">Anthony Theakston</a>, <a href="/tags/wangechi-mutu">Wangechi Mutu</a>, <a href="/tags/jeffrey-gibson">Jeffrey Gibson</a>, and more. In all, more than 50 artists are represented through 90 sculptures and installations. The pieces run the gamut of materials, from wood and stone carvings to cast bronze and resin. A group of pigeons by Maurizio Cattelan perch on structural beams and both Nichola and Anthony Theakstons&#8217; bronzes speak to the sacredness of animals, while John O&#8217;Reilly&#8217;s rendition of an emaciated female dog crouching over her pup plucks a heart-rending chord. Throughout the exhibition, emotional evocations span joy, amazement, humor, trepidation, and grief.</p>



<p>Curated by artist <a href="https://www.ericfischl.com/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Eric Fischl</a>, the show was first staged at <a href="https://www.thechurchsagharbor.org/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">The Church</a> in Sag Harbor, a historical whaling town. Now in Brooklyn, the <em>The Ark</em> lands in the former warehouse space of Powerhouse Arts, a nonprofit dedicated to fabrication and production, on the Gowanus Canal. The building is known as the &#8220;Batcave&#8221; and sits adjacent to what&#8217;s designated by the Environmental Protection Agency as a <a href="https://www.epa.gov/superfund/search-superfund-sites-where-you-live" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Superfund</a> site, a heavily polluted area in need of concerted cleanup efforts.</p>



<p>The physical location and its surroundings present a post-industrial background to a show about nature, the environment, and material exploration. Visitors are invited to walk through a room filled with animals from floor to ceiling, invoking elements of surprise and wonder. Powerhouse Arts adds, &#8220;Rather than framing environmental themes through notions of crisis and urgency alone, the exhibition centers on relationships and intimate encounters.&#8221;</p>



<p><em>The Ark </em>continues through August 30 in Brooklyn. Find more on the organization&#8217;s <a href="https://www.instagram.com/powerhouse_arts/?hl=en" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Instagram</a>.</p>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="1697" height="1206" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/ark-7.jpeg" alt="a resin sculpture of an emaciated female dog with her tail between her legs and her small, dark puppy lying on the ground below her" class="wp-image-476581" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/ark-7.jpeg 1697w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/ark-7-640x455.jpeg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/ark-7-960x682.jpeg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/ark-7-768x546.jpeg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/ark-7-1536x1092.jpeg 1536w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 1697px) 100vw, 1697px" /><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">John O’Reilly, &#8220;Intertwined&#8221; (2012), white: resin graphite; black: resin porcelain and bone powder, 24 x 21 1/2 x 31 1/2 inches (white dog), 5 x 21 1/4 x 16 1/4 inches (black dog). Photo by Gary Mamay, courtesy of Eric Fischl and April Gornik</figcaption></figure>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="2000" height="1333" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/ark-5.jpg" alt="an installation view of a bronze sculpture of a horse that looks to be made of driftwood" class="wp-image-476580" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/ark-5.jpg 2000w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/ark-5-640x427.jpg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/ark-5-960x640.jpg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/ark-5-768x512.jpg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/ark-5-1536x1024.jpg 1536w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 2000px) 100vw, 2000px" /><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">Deborah Butterfield. Installation view of &#8216;The Ark&#8217; at Powerhouse Arts, Summer 2026. Photo by Xavier Petromelis</figcaption></figure>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="1798" height="1176" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/ark-6.jpg" alt="a carving in black slate of a bird and a beetle" class="wp-image-476586" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/ark-6.jpg 1798w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/ark-6-640x419.jpg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/ark-6-960x628.jpg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/ark-6-768x502.jpg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/ark-6-1536x1005.jpg 1536w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 1798px) 100vw, 1798px" /><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">William Kent, &#8220;Bittem and Beetle&#8221; (1968), black Italian slate, 10 5/8 x 17 1/2 x 1/4 inches. Photo by Cloe Poisson, courtesy of the William Kent Art Foundation</figcaption></figure>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="2000" height="1333" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/ark-2.jpg" alt="a beaded bird sculpture by Jeffrey Gibson in 'The Ark' exhibition" class="wp-image-476577" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/ark-2.jpg 2000w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/ark-2-640x427.jpg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/ark-2-960x640.jpg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/ark-2-768x512.jpg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/ark-2-1536x1024.jpg 1536w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 2000px) 100vw, 2000px" /><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">Jeffrey Gibson. Installation view of &#8216;The Ark&#8217; at Powerhouse Arts, Summer 2026. Photo by Xavier Petromelis</figcaption></figure>

		<item>
		<title>New York City&#8217;s Last Standing Wood Column Company Closes After 110 Years</title>
		<link>https://www.thisiscolossal.com/2026/08/american-wood-column-corporation-closes/</link>
		
		<dc:creator><![CDATA[Jackie Andres]]></dc:creator>
		<pubDate>Thu, 06 Aug 2026 22:28:41 +0000</pubDate>
				<category><![CDATA[Craft]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[Film]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[History]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[architecture]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[New York City]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[sculpture]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[video]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[wood]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[woodworking]]></category>
		<guid isPermaLink="false">https://www.thisiscolossal.com/?p=476553</guid>

					<description><![CDATA[<p><img src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/americanwoodcolumncorp-13-e1786131818546.jpg" alt="New York City&#8217;s Last Standing Wood Column Company Closes After 110 Years" />"Like anything else, everything changes," says owner Thomas Lupo. "Time goes on."</p>
<p>Do stories and artists like this matter to you? Become a <a href="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/members">Colossal Member</a> today and support independent arts publishing for as little as $7 per month. The article <a href="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/2026/08/american-wood-column-corporation-closes/">New York City&#8217;s Last Standing Wood Column Company Closes After 110 Years</a> appeared first on <a href="https://www.thisiscolossal.com">Colossal</a>.</p>
]]></description>
										<content:encoded><![CDATA[<img src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/americanwoodcolumncorp-13-e1786131818546.jpg" alt="New York City&#8217;s Last Standing Wood Column Company Closes After 110 Years" />


<p>110 years ago, Thomas Lupo&#8217;s grandfather opened the American Wood Column Corporation in Brooklyn&#8217;s Williamsburg neighborhood. Specializing in architectural woodwork including decorative moulding, columns, balusters, corbels, and more, the historic family-owned company is shutting down after more than a century. A new <a href="https://youtu.be/c8svUszBVxo?si=oMoJCxdf1xzSaTrr" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">documentary</a> directed and produced by filmmaker and photographer <a href="https://www.joshuacharow.com/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Joshua Charrow</a> takes viewers on one final walk-through of the factory.</p>



<p>A vast collection of about 6,000 handmade wooden molds—many of them reverse carved molds—cover the walls and correspond to numbered samples for reference. &#8220;My grandfather bought these molds used, and they were used,&#8221; Lupo explains. &#8220;So they&#8217;ve got to be over 200 years old.&#8221;</p>



<figure class="wp-block-embed is-type-video is-provider-youtube wp-block-embed-youtube wp-embed-aspect-16-9 wp-has-aspect-ratio"><div class="wp-block-embed__wrapper">
<iframe loading="lazy" title="This Historic 110-Year-Old NYC Business Is Shutting Down" width="500" height="281" src="https://www.youtube.com/embed/c8svUszBVxo?feature=oembed" frameborder="0" allow="accelerometer; autoplay; clipboard-write; encrypted-media; gyroscope; picture-in-picture; web-share" referrerpolicy="strict-origin-when-cross-origin" allowfullscreen></iframe>
</div></figure>



<p>Throughout the film, Charrow follows Lupo around the building, documenting the owner&#8217;s favorite pieces and timeless anecdotes. Among these works are six-foot pencils, ornamental department store columns, set designs from <em>Saturday Night Live</em>, grave details from <em>The Godfather</em>, <em>The Exorcist</em> stairway, and more.</p>



<p>Filled with family stories and nostalgic memories of growing up inside a woodworking studio, Lupo is cognizant of the fact that he, too, is growing older. His team, who has been with him for close to 40 years, believe it&#8217;s also time to retire gracefully. &#8220;I will be closing down the business. It&#8217;s not a question of if, it&#8217;s a question of when. That&#8217;s all.&#8221; he says. &#8220;Like anything else, everything changes. Time goes on.&#8221;</p>



<p>Watch the full video on <a href="https://youtu.be/c8svUszBVxo?si=g7O3mzjlGSBKbT16" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">YouTube</a>.</p>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-large"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="960" height="539" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/americanwoodcolumncorp-1-960x539.jpg" alt="" class="wp-image-476554"/></figure>

		<link>https://www.thisiscolossal.com/2026/08/pure-street-photography-awards-2026-contest-winners/</link>
		
		<dc:creator><![CDATA[Kate Mothes]]></dc:creator>

				<category><![CDATA[Photography]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[contests]]></category>

		<category><![CDATA[Pure Street Photography]]></category>

					<description><![CDATA[<p><img src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/pure-street-6.jpg" alt="The Winners of the 2026 Pure Street Photography Awards Invoke Happenstance and Commotion" />Eight winners were selected from nearly 1,600 entries submitted by photographers in 50 countries.</p>
<p>Do stories and artists like this matter to you? Become a <a href="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/members">Colossal Member</a> today and support independent arts publishing for as little as $7 per month. The article <a href="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/2026/08/pure-street-photography-awards-2026-contest-winners/">The Winners of the 2026 Pure Street Photography Awards Invoke Happenstance and Commotion</a> appeared first on <a href="https://www.thisiscolossal.com">Colossal</a>.</p>

										<content:encoded><![CDATA[<img src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/pure-street-6.jpg" alt="The Winners of the 2026 Pure Street Photography Awards Invoke Happenstance and Commotion" />


<p>From happenstance and humor to solemnity and tension, the images topping the 2026 <a href="https://www.purestreetphotography.com/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Pure Street Photography Awards</a> run the gamut of daily scenes. The <a href="/tags/pure-street-photography">annual contest</a> is organized into two categories: black-and-white and open. Reflections of New York City meet dramatic views of urban spaces and pensive tableaux in rural communities, emphasizing timely and candid moments that center diverse human experiences.</p>



<p>This year, eight winners were selected from nearly 1,600 entries submitted by photographers in 50 countries. An exhibition of 158 of the top images is slated to pop up at Jawahar Kala Kendra in Jaipur, India, from November 20 to 22. The open call is also now live for the 2027 edition, and you can see more and follow updates on the competition&#8217;s <a href="https://www.instagram.com/pure.street.photography/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Instagram</a>.</p>

		<item>
		<title>A Short Film Sheds Light on the Garfield Phones Washing Up on a French Beach Since the &#8217;80s</title>
		<link>https://www.thisiscolossal.com/2026/08/silly-little-plastic-cat-short-film/</link>
		
		<dc:creator><![CDATA[Kate Mothes]]></dc:creator>
		<pubDate>Thu, 06 Aug 2026 13:39:05 +0000</pubDate>
				<category><![CDATA[Climate]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[Film]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[beach]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[ocean]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[pollution]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[pop culture]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[trash]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[video]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[Zack Grant]]></category>
		<guid isPermaLink="false">https://www.thisiscolossal.com/?p=476517</guid>

					<description><![CDATA[<p><img src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/garfield-3.jpeg" alt="A Short Film Sheds Light on the Garfield Phones Washing Up on a French Beach Since the &#8217;80s" />Breton coastal residents grew up collecting parts of a 1984 Garfield-themed plastic telephone on the beach—and still do.</p>
<p>Do stories and artists like this matter to you? Become a <a href="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/members">Colossal Member</a> today and support independent arts publishing for as little as $7 per month. The article <a href="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/2026/08/silly-little-plastic-cat-short-film/">A Short Film Sheds Light on the Garfield Phones Washing Up on a French Beach Since the &#8217;80s</a> appeared first on <a href="https://www.thisiscolossal.com">Colossal</a>.</p>
]]></description>
										<content:encoded><![CDATA[<img src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/garfield-3.jpeg" alt="A Short Film Sheds Light on the Garfield Phones Washing Up on a French Beach Since the &#8217;80s" />


<p>Amid the rugged, wave-churned shoreline of France&#8217;s Breton coast, a surprising tidbit of pop culture has kept beachcombers returning for more than 40 years. The short film &#8220;<a href="https://vimeo.com/1209564322" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Silly Little Plastic Cat</a>&#8221; transports us to this slice of Brittany, where local residents grew up collecting parts of a 1984 Garfield-themed plastic telephone on the beach—and still do. Photographer and director <a href="https://www.zackgrant.com/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Zack Grant</a>, founder the production studio <a href="https://www.2020.land/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">2020 Land</a>, was intrigued by the story, which made news a few years back after <a href="https://time.com/5561165/garfield-phones-france/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">the source</a> of the dispersed merchandise was finally discovered.</p>



<p>The part of Brittany where the phones wash up is situated along a busy shipping thoroughfare. At some point during their transit in the mid-1980s, the shipping container carrying thousands of the units fell into the sea, and over the years, its spilled contents have continued to arrive in distinctively orange, tangled jumbles. As quirky as it is, the phenomenon also shines a light on the less humorous side: the vast quantity of garbage that washes ashore.</p>



<figure class="wp-block-embed is-type-video is-provider-vimeo wp-block-embed-vimeo wp-embed-aspect-16-9 wp-has-aspect-ratio"><div class="wp-block-embed__wrapper">
<iframe loading="lazy" title="Silly Little Plastic Cat" src="https://player.vimeo.com/video/1209564322?dnt=1&amp;app_id=122963" width="500" height="281" frameborder="0" allow="autoplay; fullscreen; picture-in-picture; clipboard-write; encrypted-media; web-share" referrerpolicy="strict-origin-when-cross-origin"></iframe>
</div></figure>



<p>To put the scale of pollution into perspective, nearly 1,500 shipping containers were <a href="https://www.worldshipping.org/containers-lost-at-sea" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">lost in 2025</a> alone. Less than 10 percent of those were recovered; the rest are still missing. It&#8217;s a small fraction of the hundreds of millions of containers transported annually, yet a single 40-foot container could hold the contents of an entire three- or four-bedroom house or around 400 mattresses. Multiply that by several hundred and consider everything we ship—clothing, medical supplies, car parts, you name it—and we can start to scratch the surface of the oceans&#8217; staggering <a href="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/2022/09/ocean-cleanup-system-03/">garbage patches</a>.</p>



<p>&#8220;Silly Little Plastic Cat&#8221; illuminates the reality of pollution and also highlights how locals are motivated to help. Residents have adopted Garfield as something of a de facto mascot for cleanup projects. &#8220;We are 100 percent responsible for the current climate situation and current pollution,&#8221; says a local conservationist who aids in beach cleanups via <a href="https://www.surfrider.org/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Surfrider Foundation</a>. &#8220;We are also actors in the solutions.&#8221; Another initiative invites people to work together to regenerate older or damaged items, making them usable once again while reducing consumption.</p>



<p>See more on Grant&#8217;s work on <a href="https://vimeo.com/zackgrant" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Vimeo</a>.</p>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="2000" height="1112" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/garfield-2.jpeg" alt="a still from a short documentary about Garfield plastic phones washing up on a beach in France" class="wp-image-476519" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/garfield-2.jpeg 2000w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/garfield-2-640x356.jpeg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/garfield-2-960x534.jpeg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/garfield-2-768x427.jpeg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/garfield-2-1536x854.jpeg 1536w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 2000px) 100vw, 2000px" /></figure>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="2000" height="1108" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/garfield-1.jpeg" alt="a still from a short documentary about Garfield plastic phones washing up on a beach in France" class="wp-image-476518" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/garfield-1.jpeg 2000w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/garfield-1-640x355.jpeg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/garfield-1-960x532.jpeg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/garfield-1-768x425.jpeg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/garfield-1-1536x851.jpeg 1536w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 2000px) 100vw, 2000px" /></figure>
<p>Do stories and artists like this matter to you? Become a <a href="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/members">Colossal Member</a> today and support independent arts publishing for as little as $7 per month. The article <a href="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/2026/08/silly-little-plastic-cat-short-film/">A Short Film Sheds Light on the Garfield Phones Washing Up on a French Beach Since the &#8217;80s</a> appeared first on <a href="https://www.thisiscolossal.com">Colossal</a>.</p>
]]></content:encoded>

		<item>
		<title>Monumental Painted Wood Carvings by Jiang Miao Center Mindfulness</title>
		<link>https://www.thisiscolossal.com/2026/08/jiang-miao-spiral-of-energy-exhibition-wood-carvings-acrylic-paintings/</link>
		
		<dc:creator><![CDATA[Kate Mothes]]></dc:creator>
		<pubDate>Wed, 05 Aug 2026 18:27:00 +0000</pubDate>
				<category><![CDATA[Art]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[Jiang Miao]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[painting]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[spirituality]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[tondo]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[wood]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[woodcut]]></category>
		<guid isPermaLink="false">https://www.thisiscolossal.com/?p=476492</guid>

					<description><![CDATA[<p><img src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/miao-1.jpg" alt="Monumental Painted Wood Carvings by Jiang Miao Center Mindfulness" />Whitestone Gallery in Seoul presents the artist's solo exhibition, 'Spiral of Energy.'</p>
<p>Do stories and artists like this matter to you? Become a <a href="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/members">Colossal Member</a> today and support independent arts publishing for as little as $7 per month. The article <a href="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/2026/08/jiang-miao-spiral-of-energy-exhibition-wood-carvings-acrylic-paintings/">Monumental Painted Wood Carvings by Jiang Miao Center Mindfulness</a> appeared first on <a href="https://www.thisiscolossal.com">Colossal</a>.</p>
]]></description>
										<content:encoded><![CDATA[<img src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/miao-1.jpg" alt="Monumental Painted Wood Carvings by Jiang Miao Center Mindfulness" />


<p>The spiral is one of the most ubiquitous, universal symbols. Or perhaps it is more apt to describe the motif as mimicked from nature, where it occurs in the form of seashells, flowers, and curling waves. From Neolithic stone carvings at Newgrange in Ireland to swirling motifs on prehistoric <a href="https://asia.si.edu/whats-on/exhibitions/prehistoric-spirals-earthenware-from-thailand/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">pottery</a> discovered in Thailand, the spiral represents growth, the cycles of life, and evolution. Sometimes two or more interlink, and other times they emerge from an endless line.</p>



<p>For artist <a href="https://www.instagram.com/jiangmiao.art/?hl=en" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Jiang Miao</a>, Eastern philosophy is a touchstone. &#8220;The spiral symbolizes life, time, and the cyclical order of the universe, while color becomes a vessel for invisible energy beyond the material world,&#8221; says <a href="https://www.whitestone-gallery.com/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Whitestone Gallery</a>, which presents the artist&#8217;s solo exhibition, <em>Spiral of Energy.</em></p>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="2000" height="1987" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/miao-8.jpg" alt="an abstract wood carving with bright acrylic paint in multiple colors" class="wp-image-476499" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/miao-8.jpg 2000w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/miao-8-640x636.jpg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/miao-8-960x954.jpg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/miao-8-150x150.jpg 150w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/miao-8-768x763.jpg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/miao-8-1536x1526.jpg 1536w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 2000px) 100vw, 2000px" /><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">&#8220;Taoist Trinity and the Self&#8221; (2026), acrylic on wooden board, carving, 100 centimeters diameter</figcaption></figure>



<p>Several series are represented in the show, including <em>Heavenly Eyes, Mindfulness, Origin,</em> and <em>Taoist Trinity and the Self</em>. &#8220;<em>Heavenly Eyes</em> proposes a perspective beyond ordinary human vision, contemplating the essence of existence and the order of the universe, while <em>Mindfulness</em> explores the nature of life through introspection and awakened consciousness,&#8221; the gallery says. <em>Taoist Trinity and the Self</em> is all <a href="/tags/tondo">tondos</a> and emphasizes perpetualness. They can also be monumental: one reaches about seven feet in diameter.</p>



<p>Miao meticulously carves intricate textures into wood panels, then applies vibrant acrylic paint to create a sensorial movement, contrast, and glow. Both the approach and result are inherently concerned with time and concentration, spirituality and mindfulness.</p>



<p><em>Spiral of Energy </em>continues through August 23 in Seoul. See more on the artist&#8217;s <a href="https://www.instagram.com/jiangmiao.art/?hl=en" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Instagram</a>.</p>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="2000" height="1263" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/miao-2.jpg" alt="an abstract wood carving with bright acrylic paint in multiple colors" class="wp-image-476494" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/miao-2.jpg 2000w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/miao-2-640x404.jpg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/miao-2-960x606.jpg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/miao-2-768x485.jpg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/miao-2-1536x970.jpg 1536w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 2000px) 100vw, 2000px" /><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">&#8220;Heavenly Eyes&#8221; (2024), acrylic on aluminum panel, carving 120 x 190 centimeters</figcaption></figure>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="2000" height="2999" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/miao-9.jpg" alt="a detail of an abstract wood carving with bright acrylic paint in multiple colors" class="wp-image-476500" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/miao-9.jpg 2000w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/miao-9-640x960.jpg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/miao-9-960x1440.jpg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/miao-9-768x1152.jpg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/miao-9-1024x1536.jpg 1024w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/miao-9-1366x2048.jpg 1366w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 2000px) 100vw, 2000px" /><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">Detail</figcaption></figure>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="2000" height="2630" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/miao-4.jpg" alt="an abstract wood carving with bright acrylic paint in multiple colors" class="wp-image-476496" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/miao-4.jpg 2000w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/miao-4-640x842.jpg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/miao-4-960x1262.jpg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/miao-4-768x1010.jpg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/miao-4-1168x1536.jpg 1168w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/miao-4-1557x2048.jpg 1557w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 2000px) 100vw, 2000px" /><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">&#8220;Heavenly Eyes&#8221; (2026), acrylic on wooden board,  carving, 120 x 90 centimeters</figcaption></figure>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="2000" height="3211" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/miao-3.jpg" alt="an abstract wood carving with bright acrylic paint in multiple colors" class="wp-image-476495" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/miao-3.jpg 2000w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/miao-3-640x1028.jpg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/miao-3-960x1541.jpg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/miao-3-768x1233.jpg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/miao-3-957x1536.jpg 957w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/miao-3-1276x2048.jpg 1276w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 2000px) 100vw, 2000px" /><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">&#8220;Heavenly Eyes&#8221; (2025), acrylic on wooden board,  carving, 90 x 55 centimeters</figcaption></figure>

<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="2000" height="2441" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/miao-6.jpg" alt="an abstract wood carving with bright green acrylic paint" class="wp-image-476502" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/miao-6.jpg 2000w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/miao-6-640x781.jpg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/miao-6-960x1172.jpg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/miao-6-768x937.jpg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/miao-6-1259x1536.jpg 1259w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/miao-6-1678x2048.jpg 1678w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 2000px) 100vw, 2000px" /><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">&#8220;Mindfulness&#8221; (2023), acrylic on aluminum board, carving, 160 x 130 centimeters</figcaption></figure>

			</item>
		<item>
		<title>&#8216;Bodega Cats of New York&#8217; Advocates for the City&#8217;s Beloved Feline Shopkeepers</title>
		<link>https://www.thisiscolossal.com/2026/08/bodega-cats-of-new-york-dan-rimada-gulce-kilkis-book/</link>
		
		<dc:creator><![CDATA[Kate Mothes]]></dc:creator>
		<pubDate>Wed, 05 Aug 2026 16:00:00 +0000</pubDate>
				<category><![CDATA[Books]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[Photography]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[animals]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[cats]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[New York City]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[pets]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[stores]]></category>
		<guid isPermaLink="false">https://www.thisiscolossal.com/?p=476476</guid>

					<description><![CDATA[<p><img src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/bcny-7.jpeg" alt="&#8216;Bodega Cats of New York&#8217; Advocates for the City&#8217;s Beloved Feline Shopkeepers" />A new book from Dan Rimada, with photos by Gulce Kilkis, is slated for release in November.</p>
<p>Do stories and artists like this matter to you? Become a <a href="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/members">Colossal Member</a> today and support independent arts publishing for as little as $7 per month. The article <a href="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/2026/08/bodega-cats-of-new-york-dan-rimada-gulce-kilkis-book/">&#8216;Bodega Cats of New York&#8217; Advocates for the City&#8217;s Beloved Feline Shopkeepers</a> appeared first on <a href="https://www.thisiscolossal.com">Colossal</a>.</p>
]]></description>
										<content:encoded><![CDATA[<img src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/bcny-7.jpeg" alt="&#8216;Bodega Cats of New York&#8217; Advocates for the City&#8217;s Beloved Feline Shopkeepers" />


<p>In 2022, New York resident and bonafide feline devotee Dan Rimada felt that something needed to be done to shine a light on the city&#8217;s cats. The Big Apple not only has a real <a href="https://www.animalalliancenyc.org/about-us/nycfci/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">feral issue</a>, but many of these creatures make their homes in iconic shops found around the city: bodegas. Over time, locals get to know them and they become fixtures of shelves and countertops. Technically, though, New York City considers it a health code violation to have animals in businesses that serve food. In spite of that, thousands of cats serve as mousers and rat catchers, and a lot of people don&#8217;t realize that the snoozy tabby nestled atop the Doritos bags is actually illegal.</p>



<p>Rimada founded <a href="https://bodegacatsofnewyork.com/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Bodega Cats of New York</a> to bring visibility to these beloved, informal shop staffers. This fall, a new book published by Epic Ink titled <em>Bodega Cats of New York</em> features 120 photos of 60 cats across all five boroughs along with their stories. The images are snapped by photographer <a href="https://www.gulcekilkis.photography/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Gulce Kilkis</a>, who also runs the Instagram account <a href="https://www.instagram.com/turkish_street_cats/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">@turkish_street_cats</a>.</p>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="2000" height="2667" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/bcny-3.jpg" alt="a sleepy tabby cat in a comfy bed on the counter in a New York City bodega" class="wp-image-476479" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/bcny-3.jpg 2000w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/bcny-3-640x853.jpg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/bcny-3-960x1280.jpg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/bcny-3-768x1024.jpg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/bcny-3-1152x1536.jpg 1152w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/bcny-3-1536x2048.jpg 1536w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 2000px) 100vw, 2000px" /></figure>



<p>Advocacy is as much a part of Rimada&#8217;s mission as documenting kitties familiar to neighborhood customers, such as Oreo in Park Slope and Prince in SoHo. The type of care or attention the cats get can vary from store to store. Some are treated like royalty, while others are more like interlopers that are tolerated. Nevertheless, Rimada shares their individual stories and raises awareness of the wide range of realities for these animals.</p>



<p>Although they are still in committee, two bills facilitated by Rimada have been introduced that would &#8220;stop New York City agencies from treating a cat in a retail food store as an automatic New York City Health Code violation&#8221; along with requiring voluntary, free vaccination and spay/neuter programs. The other bill would legally allow cats in retail stores as long as they met veterinary requirements. &#8220;We want to protect what makes New York City feel like home,&#8221; Rimada says in a statement. &#8220;And that includes taking care of the cats that are a part of it.&#8221;</p>



<p><em>Bodega Cats of New York</em> is slated for release in early November. Meet hundreds more feline friends on <a href="https://www.instagram.com/newyorkbodegacats/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Instagram</a>, and pre-order your copy on the project&#8217;s <a href="https://bodegacatsofnewyork.com/book/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">website</a>. You might also enjoy Marcel Heijnen&#8217;s <em><a href="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/2025/07/marcel-heijnen-city-cats-of-istanbul/">City Cats of Istanbul</a> </em>and a trip through art history with <a href="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/2026/01/cats-art-history-book/">Phaidon&#8217;s <em>Cat</em></a><em>.</em></p>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="2000" height="2667" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/bcny-8.jpg" alt="a white and gray cat on a snack shelf in a New York City bodega" class="wp-image-476484" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/bcny-8.jpg 2000w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/bcny-8-640x853.jpg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/bcny-8-960x1280.jpg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/bcny-8-768x1024.jpg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/bcny-8-1152x1536.jpg 1152w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/bcny-8-1536x2048.jpg 1536w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 2000px) 100vw, 2000px" /></figure>

<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="2000" height="2667" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/bcny-6.jpeg" alt="a black and white cat climbing a shelf of foodstuffs in a New York City bodega" class="wp-image-476482" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/bcny-6.jpeg 2000w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/bcny-6-640x853.jpeg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/bcny-6-960x1280.jpeg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/bcny-6-768x1024.jpeg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/bcny-6-1152x1536.jpeg 1152w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/bcny-6-1536x2048.jpeg 1536w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 2000px) 100vw, 2000px" /></figure>

		<item>
		<title>Enigmatic Narratives Unfold in Aron Wiesenfeld&#8217;s Dreamy Oil Paintings</title>
		<link>https://www.thisiscolossal.com/2026/08/aron-wiesenfeld-oil-paintings-narratives/</link>
		
		<dc:creator><![CDATA[Kate Mothes]]></dc:creator>
		<pubDate>Wed, 05 Aug 2026 13:23:29 +0000</pubDate>
				<category><![CDATA[Art]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[Aron Wiesenfeld]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[narrative]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[painting]]></category>
		<guid isPermaLink="false">https://www.thisiscolossal.com/?p=476446</guid>

					<description><![CDATA[<p><img src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/wiesenfeld-5.jpg" alt="Enigmatic Narratives Unfold in Aron Wiesenfeld&#8217;s Dreamy Oil Paintings" />Wiesenfeld delves into the power of visibility and imagination.</p>
<p>Do stories and artists like this matter to you? Become a <a href="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/members">Colossal Member</a> today and support independent arts publishing for as little as $7 per month. The article <a href="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/2026/08/aron-wiesenfeld-oil-paintings-narratives/">Enigmatic Narratives Unfold in Aron Wiesenfeld&#8217;s Dreamy Oil Paintings</a> appeared first on <a href="https://www.thisiscolossal.com">Colossal</a>.</p>
]]></description>
										<content:encoded><![CDATA[<img src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/wiesenfeld-5.jpg" alt="Enigmatic Narratives Unfold in Aron Wiesenfeld&#8217;s Dreamy Oil Paintings" />


<p>Whether playing a game of Uno on the back patio by the light of a headlamp or wading into a preternaturally still body of water on a pitch-black night, the figures in <a href="https://aronwiesenfeld.com/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Aron Wiesenfeld</a>’s works calmly exist amid an air of mystery. His enigmatic <a href="/tags/aron-wiesenfeld">paintings and drawings</a> entice viewers into a world of timeless intrigue, delving into the power of visibility and imagination. Uncanny lighting creates silhouettes and deep, hidden distances. And individuals gaze at things just beyond the frame or move into unseen spaces.</p>



<p>Wiesenfeld&#8217;s vignettes are often set during dusk or in darkness, where the background gradually fades away. Many pieces summon a subtle tension, such as in &#8220;Transfer,&#8221; where a black dog looks away while a light from an obscured source shines on a mother and her child. In &#8220;Reunion,&#8221; a young boy wearing a crown gazes directly at the viewer while a solemn discussion occurs behind him.</p>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="2000" height="1376" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/wiesenfeld-8.jpg" alt="an oil painting of two young people playing Uno on a patio at night in the light of a headlamp while a dog looks on" class="wp-image-476455" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/wiesenfeld-8.jpg 2000w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/wiesenfeld-8-640x440.jpg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/wiesenfeld-8-960x660.jpg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/wiesenfeld-8-768x528.jpg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/wiesenfeld-8-1536x1057.jpg 1536w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 2000px) 100vw, 2000px" /><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">&#8220;Warm Night&#8221;</figcaption></figure>



<p>Despite the nuanced and inscrutable scenes, there is little sense of malice or danger and rather an emphasis on curiosity and the possibility of different interpretations. Wiesenfeld homes in on moments of calm communion between individuals and with nature, evoking blips from memories, dreams, and ambiguous narratives.</p>



<p>The artist has been working on a graphic novel, which will be published in France this September with the title <em>La Fuite. </em><a href="https://www.gallimard.fr/catalogue/la-fuite/9782073108005" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Pre-orders</a> for the French version are open now. Next year, it&#8217;s set for an English release, titled <em>Runoff</em>, care of <a href="https://imagecomics.com/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Image Comics</a>. See more and follow updates on the artist&#8217;s <a href="https://www.instagram.com/aronwiesenfeld/?hl=en" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Instagram</a>.</p>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="2000" height="1338" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/wiesenfeld-4.jpg" alt="an oil painting by Aron Wiesenfeld of a group of spectral women moving toward a dark cliff, with a young woman in shorts and t-shirt walking behind them" class="wp-image-476449" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/wiesenfeld-4.jpg 2000w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/wiesenfeld-4-640x428.jpg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/wiesenfeld-4-960x642.jpg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/wiesenfeld-4-768x514.jpg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/wiesenfeld-4-1536x1028.jpg 1536w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 2000px) 100vw, 2000px" /><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">Page from &#8216;Runoff&#8217;</figcaption></figure>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="2000" height="1553" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/wiesenfeld-2.jpg" alt="an oil painting by Aron Wiesenfeld of a mysterious black-and-white world with bare tree trunks and a small shoreline, where a white horse stands and a figure wades into the still water" class="wp-image-476447" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/wiesenfeld-2.jpg 2000w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/wiesenfeld-2-640x497.jpg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/wiesenfeld-2-960x745.jpg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/wiesenfeld-2-768x596.jpg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/wiesenfeld-2-1536x1193.jpg 1536w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 2000px) 100vw, 2000px" /><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">&#8220;Limbo&#8221;</figcaption></figure>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="2000" height="1799" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/wiesenfeld-3.jpg" alt="an oil painting by Aron Wiesenfeld of a white horse and rider amid an autumnal wooded scene with bare tree trunks and a ground of red leaves" class="wp-image-476448" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/wiesenfeld-3.jpg 2000w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/wiesenfeld-3-640x576.jpg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/wiesenfeld-3-960x864.jpg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/wiesenfeld-3-768x691.jpg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/wiesenfeld-3-1536x1382.jpg 1536w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 2000px) 100vw, 2000px" /><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">&#8220;Lonely Kingdom&#8221;</figcaption></figure>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="2000" height="1493" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/wiesenfeld-6.jpg" alt="an oil painting by Aron Wiesenfeld of a mother and daughter in an open landscape near a tree, lit up perhaps by a headline, with a black dog nearby" class="wp-image-476451" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/wiesenfeld-6.jpg 2000w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/wiesenfeld-6-640x478.jpg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/wiesenfeld-6-960x717.jpg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/wiesenfeld-6-768x573.jpg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/wiesenfeld-6-1536x1147.jpg 1536w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 2000px) 100vw, 2000px" /><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">&#8220;Transfer&#8221;</figcaption></figure>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="2000" height="1612" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/wiesenfeld-1.jpg" alt="an oil painting by Aron Wiesenfeld of a silhouetted figure on a bicycle heading into a dimly lit entrance of a darkened tunnel" class="wp-image-476453" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/wiesenfeld-1.jpg 2000w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/wiesenfeld-1-640x516.jpg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/wiesenfeld-1-960x774.jpg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/wiesenfeld-1-768x619.jpg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/wiesenfeld-1-1536x1238.jpg 1536w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 2000px) 100vw, 2000px" /><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">&#8220;Entrance&#8221;</figcaption></figure>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="2000" height="1671" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/wiesenfeld-9.jpg" alt="an oil painting by Aron Wiesenfeld of a tiny figure standing on a bed, looking out the window at a full-size human boy looking back in" class="wp-image-476454" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/wiesenfeld-9.jpg 2000w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/wiesenfeld-9-640x535.jpg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/wiesenfeld-9-960x802.jpg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/wiesenfeld-9-768x642.jpg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/wiesenfeld-9-1536x1283.jpg 1536w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 2000px) 100vw, 2000px" /><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">&#8220;Window&#8221;</figcaption></figure>

		<item>
		<title>Tiny Faces Surface Amid Sweeping Lines in En Iwamura&#8217;s Expressive Sculptures</title>
		<link>https://www.thisiscolossal.com/2026/08/en-iwamura-expressive-ceramic-sculptures/</link>
		
		<dc:creator><![CDATA[Grace Ebert]]></dc:creator>
		<pubDate>Tue, 04 Aug 2026 18:50:05 +0000</pubDate>
				<category><![CDATA[Art]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[ceramics]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[emotions]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[En Iwamura]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[faces]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[sculpture]]></category>
		<guid isPermaLink="false">https://www.thisiscolossal.com/?p=476456</guid>

					<description><![CDATA[<p><img src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/iwamura-1.jpg" alt="Tiny Faces Surface Amid Sweeping Lines in En Iwamura&#8217;s Expressive Sculptures" />En Iwamura is interested in the ways we measure and understand the spaces between ourselves and others.</p>
<p>Do stories and artists like this matter to you? Become a <a href="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/members">Colossal Member</a> today and support independent arts publishing for as little as $7 per month. The article <a href="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/2026/08/en-iwamura-expressive-ceramic-sculptures/">Tiny Faces Surface Amid Sweeping Lines in En Iwamura&#8217;s Expressive Sculptures</a> appeared first on <a href="https://www.thisiscolossal.com">Colossal</a>.</p>
]]></description>
										<content:encoded><![CDATA[<img src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/iwamura-1.jpg" alt="Tiny Faces Surface Amid Sweeping Lines in En Iwamura&#8217;s Expressive Sculptures" />


<p>In the voluptuous ceramics of <a href="https://www.instagram.com/eniwamura" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">En Iwamura</a>, sweeping lines of clay frame minuscule eyes and noses that just barely emerge from the earthen material. The artist is based in the iconic pottery town of <a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shigaraki,_Shiga" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Shigaraki</a> in Japan&#8217;s Shiga Prefecture and is known for his expressive yet abstract sculptures. Evoking playful depictions of masks and busts, the works are often vibrant in color, featuring bold gradients or two-toned combinations.</p>



<p>Iwamura has long drawn on the concept of Ma, or “間,” which translates to gap or pause. In the artist&#8217;s practice, the idea appears both conceptually and holistically. He&#8217;s interested in the ways we measure and understand the spaces between ourselves and others and how those conceptions appear in our expressions. Viewers can explore the gaps between themselves and individual works or consider how groups of characters interact, each time negotiating a dynamic emotional terrain.</p>



<p>Find more from Iwamura and peek into his studio on <a href="https://www.instagram.com/eniwamura" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Instagram</a>.</p>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="2000" height="1333" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/iwamura-6.jpg" alt="a collection of abstract ceramic sculptures by en iwamura with a tiny face" class="wp-image-476463" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/iwamura-6.jpg 2000w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/iwamura-6-640x427.jpg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/iwamura-6-960x640.jpg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/iwamura-6-768x512.jpg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/iwamura-6-1536x1024.jpg 1536w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 2000px) 100vw, 2000px" /></figure>

<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="2000" height="2000" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/iwamura-3.jpg" alt="an abstract ceramic sculpture by en iwamura with a tiny face" class="wp-image-476460" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/iwamura-3.jpg 2000w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/iwamura-3-640x640.jpg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/iwamura-3-960x960.jpg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/iwamura-3-150x150.jpg 150w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/iwamura-3-768x768.jpg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/iwamura-3-1536x1536.jpg 1536w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 2000px) 100vw, 2000px" /></figure>

		<item>
		<title>Lydia Hansen Introduces Hikers to Native Midwest Mushrooms on Crocheted &#8216;Fungi Hunts&#8217;</title>
		<link>https://www.thisiscolossal.com/2026/08/lydia-hansen-fungi-hunts-crocheted-mushrooms-minnesota/</link>
		
		<dc:creator><![CDATA[Kate Mothes]]></dc:creator>
		<pubDate>Tue, 04 Aug 2026 15:33:03 +0000</pubDate>
				<category><![CDATA[Craft]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[Nature]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[forests]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[fungi]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[Lydia Hansen]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[mushrooms]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[public art]]></category>
		<guid isPermaLink="false">https://www.thisiscolossal.com/?p=476432</guid>

					<description><![CDATA[<p><img src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/hansen-5.jpg" alt="Lydia Hansen Introduces Hikers to Native Midwest Mushrooms on Crocheted &#8216;Fungi Hunts&#8217;" />An ongoing series of seasonal scavenger hunts in Minnesota woodlands playfully invite inquiry.</p>
<p>Do stories and artists like this matter to you? Become a <a href="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/members">Colossal Member</a> today and support independent arts publishing for as little as $7 per month. The article <a href="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/2026/08/lydia-hansen-fungi-hunts-crocheted-mushrooms-minnesota/">Lydia Hansen Introduces Hikers to Native Midwest Mushrooms on Crocheted &#8216;Fungi Hunts&#8217;</a> appeared first on <a href="https://www.thisiscolossal.com">Colossal</a>.</p>
]]></description>
										<content:encoded><![CDATA[<img src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/hansen-5.jpg" alt="Lydia Hansen Introduces Hikers to Native Midwest Mushrooms on Crocheted &#8216;Fungi Hunts&#8217;" />


<p>In 2023, Minnesota-based artist <a href="https://www.lydiahansen.art/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Lydia Hansen</a> set a goal of taking at least one hike every week throughout the entire year to care for her mental health. She began musing about how fun it would be to create crocheted mushrooms that one would encounter with the same surprise they&#8217;d feel coming across the real thing. Serendipitously, she ran into one of the trail managers of the park she was exploring and shared her idea. &#8220;That turned into my very first <em>Fungi Hunt</em>, which ran for an entire year at the Lost Creek Hiking Trail near Chatfield, Minnesota,&#8221; the artist tells Colossal.</p>



<p>This summer marks the third iteration of the project, which visitors can explore at <a href="https://eaglebluffmn.org/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Eagle Bluff Environmental Learning Center</a> in Lanesboro, Minnesota, and Hansen already has more planned for the next couple of seasons. The artist describes her practice as &#8220;experiential fiber art,&#8221; combining her love of nature and creativity in the public sphere. &#8220;When I was developing the <em>Fungi Hunt</em>, one of the motivating factors behind the design was to create something that would encourage people to be looking up from their feet and taking note of what was around them as they walked,&#8221; she says.</p>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="2000" height="1562" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/hansen-6.jpg" alt="a crocheted version of Turkey tail fungi on a stump in woods in Minnesota" class="wp-image-476434" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/hansen-6.jpg 2000w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/hansen-6-640x500.jpg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/hansen-6-960x750.jpg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/hansen-6-768x600.jpg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/hansen-6-1536x1200.jpg 1536w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 2000px) 100vw, 2000px" /><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">Turkey tail</figcaption></figure>



<p>Each crocheted oyster mushroom or turkey tail is a nod to native flora of the region. &#8220;The point of this &#8216;restriction&#8217; is to highlight what&#8217;s already around us, not just the most colorful, most unusual, or most oddball fungi species the world has to offer—and there are many weirdo fungi out there,&#8221; Hansen says. She uses secondhand yarn for the mushrooms themselves, then she staples, screws, or stakes the pieces temporarily onto dead wood.</p>



<p>A grant from the Southeastern Minnesota Arts Council supports the Eagle Bluff project and allowed Hansen to contract Minnesota naturalist and “fellow fungi nerd” Tanner Barnharst to develop interpretive signage. &#8220;As the internet gets rapidly more unreliable to accurate scientific information, I wanted to make sure folks could get good information on the hikes—especially since cell service is spotty on a lot of these trails,&#8221; the artist says.</p>



<p>The Eagle Bluff <em>Fungi Hunt </em>continues through October 31. If you&#8217;re in the area, Hansen and Barnharst will be leading a free guided mycology hike in the afternoon of August 16. The artist is currently preparing for her largest hunt yet, which will take place across three parks in Olmsted County next summer. She&#8217;s also curating a fungi-themed exhibition at <a href="https://koubagallery.org/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Kouba Gallery</a> in Bloomington, Minnesota, and is excited to be fielding invitations from further afield for future installations.</p>



<p>See more on Hansen&#8217;s <a href="https://www.instagram.com/lydiahansen.art/">Instagram</a>.</p>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="2000" height="1999" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/hansen-4.jpg" alt="a trio of crocheted mushrooms on a tree in woods in Minnesota" class="wp-image-476439" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/hansen-4.jpg 2000w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/hansen-4-640x640.jpg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/hansen-4-960x960.jpg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/hansen-4-150x150.jpg 150w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/hansen-4-768x768.jpg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/hansen-4-1536x1536.jpg 1536w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 2000px) 100vw, 2000px" /><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">Pheasantback</figcaption></figure>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="2000" height="2667" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/hansen-3.jpg" alt="a trio of crocheted mushrooms on a tree in woods in Minnesota" class="wp-image-476438" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/hansen-3.jpg 2000w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/hansen-3-640x853.jpg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/hansen-3-960x1280.jpg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/hansen-3-768x1024.jpg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/hansen-3-1152x1536.jpg 1152w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/hansen-3-1536x2048.jpg 1536w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 2000px) 100vw, 2000px" /><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">Oyster mushroom</figcaption></figure>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="2000" height="1499" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/hansen-1.jpg" alt="" class="wp-image-476436" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/hansen-1.jpg 2000w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/hansen-1-640x480.jpg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/hansen-1-960x720.jpg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/hansen-1-768x576.jpg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/hansen-1-1536x1151.jpg 1536w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 2000px) 100vw, 2000px" /><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">Giant puffball</figcaption></figure>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="2000" height="2667" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/hansen-2.jpg" alt="a cluster of crocheted golden mushrooms on a tree in woods in Minnesota" class="wp-image-476437" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/hansen-2.jpg 2000w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/hansen-2-640x853.jpg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/hansen-2-960x1280.jpg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/hansen-2-768x1024.jpg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/hansen-2-1152x1536.jpg 1152w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/hansen-2-1536x2048.jpg 1536w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 2000px) 100vw, 2000px" /><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">Golden oyster</figcaption></figure>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="2000" height="2667" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/hansen-7.jpg" alt="a cluster of crocheted golden mushrooms on a tree in woods in Minnesota with a sign denoting it's Chicken of the Woods" class="wp-image-476435" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/hansen-7.jpg 2000w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/hansen-7-640x853.jpg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/hansen-7-960x1280.jpg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/hansen-7-768x1024.jpg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/hansen-7-1152x1536.jpg 1152w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/hansen-7-1536x2048.jpg 1536w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 2000px) 100vw, 2000px" /><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">Chicken of the woods</figcaption></figure>
